title: Exact comparisons are detected on approximations with increasingly connective tails
statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category], let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], and fix its unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal A)$ with cohomology functors $H^d$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $F,G:\mathcal T\to D(\mathcal A)$ be exact functors with specified shift isomorphisms, and let $e:F\Rightarrow G$ be a natural transformation compatible with these isomorphisms, so that it gives a morphism between the image distinguished triangles. Fix $K\in\mathcal T$. For every $n\in\mathbf Z$, suppose given a distinguished triangle $A_n\xrightarrow{i_n}K\to E_n\to A_n[1]$. Suppose $e_{A_n}$ is an isomorphism for every $n$, and suppose there exists a single integer $c$ such that for every $n$ and $r\le n-c$ one has $H^r(F(E_n))=H^r(G(E_n))=0$. Then $e_K:F(K)\to G(K)$ is an isomorphism. More precisely, for every $d\in\mathbf Z$ and every $n\ge d+c$, both $H^d(F(i_n))$ and $H^d(G(i_n))$ are isomorphisms, and
$$H^d(e_K)=H^d(G(i_n))\circ H^d(e_{A_n})\circ H^d(F(i_n))^{-1}.$$
No boundedness of $K$, no compatibility maps between different $A_n$, and no preservation of infinite limits or colimits is assumed.

proof.text: Fix $d\in\mathbf Z$ and $n\ge d+c$. Then $d-1\le d\le n-c$. For each $J\in\{F,G\}$, exactness of $J$ sends the given triangle to a distinguished triangle $J(A_n)\xrightarrow{J(i_n)}J(K)\to J(E_n)\to J(A_n)[1]$. The long exact cohomology sequence gives the exact segment $H^{d-1}(J(E_n))\to H^d(J(A_n))\xrightarrow{H^d(J(i_n))}H^d(J(K))\to H^d(J(E_n))$. Both outside terms are zero by the tail hypothesis. Thus the middle arrow has zero kernel and cokernel, hence is mono and epi. To spell out invertibility in the abelian category: a mono $a$ is a kernel of some $b$; since $a$ is epi and $ba=0$, $b=0$, and the universal property of its kernel identifies $a$ with the identity kernel of the zero map. Consequently $H^d(F(i_n))$ and $H^d(G(i_n))$ are isomorphisms.

proof.text: Naturality of $e$ at $i_n:A_n\to K$ says $e_K\circ F(i_n)=G(i_n)\circ e_{A_n}$. Apply the cohomology functor $H^d$ and compose on the right with $H^d(F(i_n))^{-1}$ from Step 1. Functoriality gives precisely $H^d(e_K)=H^d(G(i_n))\circ H^d(e_{A_n})\circ H^d(F(i_n))^{-1}$. The middle factor is invertible: applying $H^d$ to the two inverse identities for $e_{A_n}$ gives its inverse $H^d(e_{A_n}^{-1})$. All three factors are therefore isomorphisms, so $H^d(e_K)$ is an isomorphism for every $n\ge d+c$.

proof.text: For every integer $d$ take $n=d+c$. Step 2 proves that $H^d(e_K)$ is an isomorphism. The cohomology criterion for the unbounded derived category now implies that $e_K$ is an isomorphism. This argument chooses a separate approximation for each degree and uses no relations between the $A_n$, no boundedness of $K$, and no infinite limit or colimit.
